description.narrative: (Bangladesh): The Promoting Advocacy and Rights (PAR) activity works to strengthen the capacity of civil-society to advocate for improved democratic governance and establish partnerships to improve government responsiveness to citizens' needs. USAID provides local organizations with grants to build their advocacy capabilities and supports the advocacy efforts of coalitions of civil society organizations (CSOs) and local government agencies to address community problems, such as gender-based violence, drug addiction, environmental pollution, and unplanned urbanization. The advocacy model involves an initial community survey in which CSOs and citizens prioritize social concerns or community problems. CSOs then form a coalition of stakeholders, including local government agencies, and then develop a charter of action to collectively advocate for change and to address a specific social issue or community problem. USAID will continue to provide CSOs with technical support so they can conduct a variety of strategic advocacy campaigns with the goal of increasing the confidence of citizens in their local government's ability to resolve community problems. USAID will also provide CSOs with digital security tools to help them learn about their legal rights and compliance responsibilities. This IM contributes to meeting the required GBV ($200K), Child Marriage ($1M), DRG ($1.7M), and Freedom of Expression ($300K) earmarks. This activity will be in line with the State-USAID Integrated Country Strategy (ICS) Mission Goal Two and the U.S. government development objective of enhanced opportunities for an inclusive, healthy, educated society, and a robust economy.. .
